chunks: My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) who said: Ali ibn al-Hussein al-Sa'd Abady narrated from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah al-Barqi, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:
Whoever earns wealth through illegitimate means, God will make a building, water, and clay rule over him.
ai.seo_question: What is the divine consequence for earning wealth through illegitimate means?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), linking illicit wealth to specific natural calamities—fire, flood, and burial—that serve as tangible signs of divine retribution. This narration underscores the concept of *tadbir ilahi* (divine management), where the very elements of creation are mobilized to correct the spiritual imbalance caused by *ghabn* or *haram* in one's sustenance. It serves as a practical warning for believers to ensure the purity of their income to maintain harmony with the natural world.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 3-205 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Ali ibn al-Hussein al-Sa’ed Abady quoted on the authority of Ahmad ibn Aba Abdullah al-Barqy, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, on the authority of Hisham ibn al-Hakam that Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB) said, “
God will make a building, water and clay rule over whoever gains property through illegitimate means.”
